I write a fair bit on individual sovereignty, and it ties in here.

As far as this goes, there's arguably really only one significant point on which to divide humans - those who respect the individual sovereignty of others and those who don't. If one focuses on that aspect of human interaction, then all the rest of the things over which people divide become meaningless. If one respects the individual sovereignty of others, then it doesn't matter in the least if one is a christian or a muslim or a jew or an atheist or a democrat or a republican or a liberal or a conservative or a capitalist or a socialist or... whatever. The harm never comes from the mere fact that individuals identify as any of those things. The harm ALWAYS comes when those individuals refuse to respect the individual sovereignty of others - when they condemn and/or attack others for exercising their own individual sovereignty to adopt a different identification.

And really it's not, or more accurately shouldn't be, a particularly noteworthy distinction. It is, in fact, a thing that we all recognize at some level, at least with more concrete issues. It's so fundamental and so broadly understood that it's the exact thing that distinguishes criminal acts. The thief isn't a thief because he's come into possession of the property of another - he's a thief because he's come into possession of the property of another contrary to the will of the other. The rapist isn't a rapist because he's had sex with another - he's a rapist because he's had sex with another contrary to the will of the other. And so on. In all such cases, the exact thing that distinguishes the illegal act is the fact that it's an act taken contrary to the will of another - it's a violation of the individual sovereignty of another. And in fact, that's the exact definition of a "victim" - that's what characterizes any victim of any wrong - the victim is the one whose individual sovereignty has been violated.

Somehow though, in spite of the fact that that's the exact point on which we generally distinguish wrong, most seem to remain completely oblivious to its significance.
